clue.text: All right for light and water?

parts.note: a Very light is a coloured signal flare fired from a pistol, named after its inventor
a well is a source of water drawn from the ground

explanation.surface: Someone approves of a plan to supply a house with lighting and water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very' comes from the Very light, a flare; 'for' and 'and' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'very well' expresses agreement, just as 'all right' does.

clue.text: It tastes sweet, but schoolboys dislike it

definitions.meaning: sugar is refined from a tall sweet grass stem
a rod once used to beat pupils as punishment

explanation.surface: A treat that children nonetheless hate.
explanation.definitionFit: Sugar comes from a sweet grass stalk, and a rod of that name was the old school punishment.

clue.text: Stress injury

definitions.meaning: pressure or tension placed on something
a pulled muscle or overstretched ligament

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both tension or pressure and a muscle injury from overexertion.

clue.text: The country bears it in mind

indicators.note: in means the word it sits inside the word for mind

parts.note: the brain is the organ of the mind
taken as written

explanation.surface: A nation remembers something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bears' is a link word: the brain holds IT inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Britain is a country, the UK's island nation.

clue.text: I'll put my production to increase

indicators.note: a production makes something new out of these letters, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Someone vows to boost their output.
explanation.definitionFit: To multiply is to increase greatly in number.

clue.text: Reach the others and stop

parts.note: to come to a place is to reach it
the rest means the remaining others

explanation.surface: Catching up with the group and then halting.
explanation.definitionFit: To come to rest is an idiom for halting or ceasing motion.

clue.text: A comparison which makes one break into a grin

indicators.note: the word for one breaks into the middle of the grin word

parts.note: a grin is a broad smile
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Some comparison is so apt it makes the listener smile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'which makes' is a link; 'break into a grin' is also a phrase meaning start smiling.
explanation.definitionFit: A simile is a figure of speech comparing two things with 'like' or 'as'.

clue.text: Beckham, say, swayed games on pitch

indicators.note: on means the first piece goes on top of, before, the second
swayed means moved about, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: pitch is the black sticky substance tar

explanation.surface: A footballer influences the outcome of matches on the field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swayed' rearranges GAMES into MEGAS; 'pitch' looks like a football field but is TAR.
explanation.definitionFit: David Beckham is an example of a huge celebrity, a superstar of football.

clue.text: More work here?

parts.note: reads as asking for extra labour, but means the book written by Sir Thomas More and the ideal place it depicts

explanation.definitionFit: Thomas More's best-known work describes an imaginary ideal commonwealth.

clue.text: Old town subject to inflation

definitions.meaning: an ancient Phoenician city in what is now Lebanon
a car wheel's rubber covering is pumped up with air

explanation.definitionFit: It names both the ancient Phoenician port and the inflatable rubber ring on a wheel (British spelling).

clue.text: Is hesitant when perplexed? Quite the contrary

indicators.note: perplexed means confused, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone dithers when puzzled, or perhaps does just the opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: An antithesis is the direct opposite of something, the complete contrary.

clue.text: Not how Anne Boleyn's ghost will collide with you

definitions.text: Not how Anne Boleyn's ghost will collide with you

parts.words: Not how Anne Boleyn's ghost will collide with you
parts.note: the beheaded queen's ghost is said to carry her head under her arm, so it cannot meet you face-first

explanation.surface: A warning about bumping into a famous ghost.
explanation.walkthrough: Anne Boleyn, a wife of Henry VIII, was beheaded; her ghost is pictured with her head tucked under her arm.
explanation.definitionFit: A head-on collision is a frontal one, with the front parts striking directly.

clue.text: Attendant who never answers back gets pushed around

definitions.text: Attendant who never answers back gets pushed around

parts.words: Attendant who never answers back gets pushed around
parts.note: reads as a meek silent servant, but means a small serving lift or a revolving stand of shelves

explanation.definitionFit: This is a small lift or rotating tray that serves food, a silent mechanical servant.

clue.text: I am conclusively shown to be better

parts.note: I'm is the short form of I am
something conclusively shown has been proved

explanation.surface: Someone claims they have been demonstrated to be superior.
explanation.definitionFit: Improved means made better or grown better than before.

clue.text: A big hit, poetry, that is fashionable

parts.note: to lam is to strike hard
an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: A hit song or a poem said to be very trendy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that is' is a link word; 'big hit' looks like a chart success but is LAM, a hard blow.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase, borrowed into English, means in the current style.

clue.text: The length of time around it varies

indicators.note: varies means changes, so these letters change order

explanation.surface: How long it takes to get round something is not fixed.
explanation.definitionFit: Duration is how long something lasts, the time it occupies.

clue.text: The sort ready to compose something impressive?

parts.note: a sort is a type or kind
set means ready, as in 'get set'

explanation.surface: A kind of person prepared to create something grand.
explanation.walkthrough: In printing, to compose is to set text in type, and printing makes impressions on paper, hence 'impressive'.
explanation.definitionFit: Printers' compositors arrange type to make printed impressions.

clue.text: Weather men caught in a flurry of sleet

indicators.note: caught in means the men are held inside the other letters
a flurry is a swirl, so these letters whirl about

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Forecasters are caught out by a sudden sleet shower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Weather men' reads as forecasters, but the definition is just 'Weather'. 'a flurry of' makes ELETS, which 'caught in' wraps around the men.
explanation.definitionFit: The elements are wind, rain and other weather forces collectively.

clue.text: I have to go ashore in a ship when visiting them

definitions.text: I have to go ashore in a ship when visiting them

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in means landing sits inside the letters for a ship

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
to land is to go ashore

explanation.surface: A traveller explains that touring these places means disembarking from a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'have to' is a link word. The whole clue is also the definition: you reach these places by ship and land.
explanation.definitionFit: Islands are pieces of land surrounded by water, visited by sea.

clue.text: A few stiff doubles needed before opening this show

definitions.text: A few stiff doubles needed before opening this show

parts.words: A few stiff doubles needed before opening this show
parts.note: sounds like strong drinks for nerves, but means rigid lifelike figures of celebrities on display

explanation.definitionFit: This is an exhibition of wax models of famous people, rigid lookalikes.

clue.text: An aggressive female runner

definitions.meaning: a fierce warrior woman of Greek legend
a river, which runs, the great South American one

explanation.definitionFit: It names both the mythical warrior women and the South American river.

clue.text: Chortle when sober man gets into a row

indicators.note: gets into means one piece enters the other

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats
TT, teetotal, describes a non-drinker

explanation.surface: A teetotaller laughs on joining a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' looks like an argument but is a tier of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: A titter is a suppressed giggle, close to a chortle.

clue.text: To step up will protect the foot

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a pace is a step

explanation.surface: Advice that stepping up a gear needs footwear protection.
explanation.definitionFit: A toecap is the reinforced front of a boot that shields the toes.

clue.text: Justice obtained by a soldier in various matters

indicators.note: in means the soldier piece goes inside the rearranged letters
various means diverse, so these letters are mixed

parts.note: GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: Justice is achieved by a soldier in several affairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Justice' looks like a quality but is a title for a judge. 'obtained by' is a link; 'various' makes MSTRATE, and 'in' puts the soldier inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A magistrate is a justice of the peace who tries minor cases.

clue.text: Hear athlete is puffed

indicators.note: hear means the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: a Blue is a sportsperson who has represented Oxford or Cambridge University

explanation.surface: Listen: the runner is out of breath.
explanation.definitionFit: Blew and puffed both mean exhaled air hard.

clue.text: Raise game although ready to drop

definitions.meaning: ... drive birds from cover on a shoot

explanation.definitionFit: To beat is to flush birds for shooting, and 'beat' also means exhausted.

clue.text: Looted overthrown city of Spain

indicators.note: overthrown means upset, so these letters are turned about

explanation.surface: A Spanish city sacked and conquered.
explanation.definitionFit: Toledo is a historic city in central Spain.

clue.text: Exceptionally animated, sparkling stuff

indicators.note: exceptionally means in an unusual way, so these letters are arranged unusually

explanation.surface: Something that glitters in a very lively way.
explanation.definitionFit: Diamante is fabric or decoration glittering with sequins or paste gems.
